data.name: Hrithansh
data.gender_notes: Hrithansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hrithansh is a Sanskrit name, derived from the Sanskrit words 'Hritha' meaning 'manifestation' and 'Ansh' meaning 'god'. The name signifies the manifestation of a god. The name Hrithansh carries the meaning “God's manifestation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hrithansh usually hope their child will grow to embody god's manifestation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine blessings and protection of Lord Vishnu.
data.etymology: Hrithansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's manifestation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hrithansh total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Hrithansh was a renowned mathematician, astronomer, and philosopher of ancient India. He is believed to have lived during the Gupta Empire (approximately 320-550 AD). He is best known for his work 'Bhaskara-Sutra', which contains advanced mathematical concepts such as the concept of zero and the adoption of the decimal positional notation system.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Hrithansh, also known as Bhaskara II, is as a 12th-century astronomer. He wrote several works on astronomy, most notably 'Siddhanta Shiromani'. This work contained a table of astronomical constants which enabled accurate predictions of planetary positions. This work was influential in the development of astronomical sciences in India and beyond.
